outline.description: Introduce the landscape of large foundation models, the need for efficient adaptation, and the major paradigms of parameter‑efficient finetuning (PEFT).  This chapter situates Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) within the broader PEFT narrative.
subtopics: Large foundation models and scalability challenges
Three PEFT families: weight‑finetuning, adapters, and prompts
Motivation for preserving pretrained knowledge
Overview of related work: LoRA, BitFit, etc.

outline.description: Explain the core idea of OFT: transforming neurons within a layer by a shared orthogonal matrix to preserve pairwise angles.  Covers reparameterization, Cayley parameterization, and the block‑diagonal implementation that balances expressiveness and parameter budget.
subtopics: OFT objective and its relation to spectral norm preservation
Cayley parameterization of orthogonal matrices
Block‑diagonal OFT: construction, zero‑initialization, trainable parameters
Empirical advantages over additive updates (LoRA)

outline.description: Characterize why a dense orthogonal matrix requires O(d²) parameters, contrast with block‑diagonal savings, and formalize the desiderata for a compact yet expressive orthogonal transform.
subtopics: Parameter count in dense vs block‑diagonal OFT
Costs of fixed sparsity patterns
Expressivity vs regularity trade‑off

outline.chapter_title: 4. Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Introduce a novel viewpoint: viewing the synthesis of a dense orthogonal matrix as transmitting information over a grid graph formed by successive sparse matrices.
subtopics: Grid‑structured graph representation of matrix multiplication
Directed edges as non‑zero entries and connectivity constraints
Dense connectivity requirement for full matrix generation
Counting free edges vs parameter efficiency

outline.chapter_title: 5. Butterfly Structures – From FFT to Efficient Orthogonal Parameterization
outline.description: Present butterfly graphs derived from Cooley–Tukey FFT as an efficient topology that achieves dense connectivity with only O(d log d) edges.
subtopics: Cooley–Tukey recursive factorization and butterfly factor definition
Recursive construction of d‑dimensional butterfly matrices
Butterfly component as block‑diagonal factor with 2×2 blocks
Ensuring orthogonality via Cayley transform on each 2×2 block

outline.description: Define BOFT as an exponentiated product of orthogonal butterfly components.  Detail initialization, dropout variant, hyperparameters (m,b), and computational complexity.
subtopics:
Formulation of R(m,b)=Π_i 	ilde{B}^b_{(d,i)}
Identity initialization
Multiplicative Dropout (block & component masking)
Parameter count: ½(b-1)d m effective parameters
Special cases: BOFT(1,b)=block‑diagonal OFT; BOFT(1,d)=full OFT; BOFT(log d,2)=full butterfly

outline.chapter_title: 7. Theoretical Insights into BOFT Expressivity & Stability
outline.description: Discuss why BOFT subsumes OFT, expressiveness gains over block structures, spectral properties conferred by left multiplication with an orthogonal matrix, and connections to bilinear similarity learning.
subtopics:
Theorem 4.1 – BOFT more expressive than OFT (same block size)
Generalized orthogonal composition → full orthogonal group (kaleidoscope hierarchy)
Spectral norm preservation advantages over LoRA
BOFT as bilinear similarity learning
